Task: APRV-376.

## What this is

`approval status` gains an informational `refusals` field and row covering both `audit.decision_refused` (APRV-235) and `audit.gesture_refused` (APRV-355) at once, so an operator told that taps from an unmapped account are being refused can see how many and from which account without reading the chain.

- JSON: `refusals: { decision?: {count, recent[]}, gesture?: {count, recent[]} }`, each `recent` entry `{seq, code, sender?}`, newest first, capped at five. The sender is reported in the record's own form, so a keyed digest (APRV-370) keeps its `hashed` marker.
- Human rendering: one row, `refusals  1 decision, 1 gesture (reported; health unaffected)`, with one line per recent entry under it.
- Informational: moves neither `healthy` nor the exit code. A family with no records is absent, and so is the whole object when both are, so a log with no refusals emits byte-identical output.
- Event names are matched as string literals rather than importing the two writer modules, so the module-graph suites that pin "no enforcement path reads this record" need no exemption.

SPEC 11.1 invariants touched: 1 (verified read only; a tampering test asserts the field disappears on a log that does not verify) and 6 (codes copied verbatim, no third copy of either union).
